title: Engineering cryogenic setups for 100-qubit scale superconducting circuit systems
authors: Sebastian Krinner; Simon Storz; Philipp Kurpiers; Paul Magnard; Johannes Heinsoo; Raphael Keller; Janis Luetolf; Christopher Eichler; Andreas Wallraff
supports: EPJ Quantum Technology 6, 2 (2019), doi 10.1140/epjqt/s40507-019-0072-0. Drive, flux and output lines; ~60 dB drive attenuation for ~1e-3 noise photons; up to 10 qubits per multiplexed readout line; Table 1 stage cooling powers (30 W at 45 K, 1.5 W at 4.2 K, 40 mW at 1.2 K, 200 µW at 140 mK, 19 µW at 20 mK); Table 2 measured passive loads per drive and flux line; 0.050 µW average DC flux-bias load per line at MXC; 124 RF lines for 50 qubits; 25 lines per port, six ports; ~30% largest load at CP and MXC for 50 qubits; thermal budget for ~150 qubits; ~400 and ~1000-qubit scenarios.

title: Cryo-CMOS Circuits and Systems for Quantum Computing Applications
authors: Bishnu Patra; Rosario M. Incandela; Jeroen P. G. van Dijk; Harald A. R. Homulle; Lin Song; Mina Shahmohammadi; Robert Bogdan Staszewski; Andrei Vladimirescu; Masoud Babaie; Fabio Sebastiano; Edoardo Charbon
supports: IEEE J. Solid-State Circuits 53(1), 309–321 (2018). Case for cryo-CMOS control (down to 4 K) for large-scale quantum computers; demonstrated LNA for spin-qubit RF-reflectometry readout and a class-F2,3 DCO.
note: Abstract and bibliographic record checked via TU Delft repository page and Crossref; full text not read.

title: Design and Characterization of a 28-nm Bulk-CMOS Cryogenic Quantum Controller Dissipating Less Than 2 mW at 3 K
supports: IEEE J. Solid-State Circuits 54(11), 3043–3060 (2019). Cryogenic CMOS XY controller for transmons at 3 K; under 2 mW total power; digital stream under 500 Mb/s.
note: Abstract via Google Research publication page; number of qubits per controller not checked.

title: Physical qubit calibration on a directed acyclic graph
authors: Julian Kelly; Peter O'Malley; Matthew Neeley; Hartmut Neven; John M. Martinis
supports: arXiv 1803.03226 (2018), preprint. Calibration as a DAG of nodes with tolerance and timeout; check state / check data / calibrate; maintain and diagnose traversals; unrolling cycles into precision layers.
note: Preprint only; same paper as listed in the decision-path spec.

title: Fluctuations of Energy-Relaxation Times in Superconducting Qubits
supports: Phys. Rev. Lett. 121, 090502 (2018). T1 varies by up to an order of magnitude, with changes on 15-minute timescales and across 5 MHz, attributed mainly to TLS defects; qubit-frequency calibration stable within ±1 MHz over ~25 h in their setup.

title: IBM Sets the Course to Build World's First Large-Scale, Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computer at New IBM Quantum Data Center
supports: Press release, 10 June 2025. Starling by 2029 in Poughkeepsie: 100 million quantum operations on 200 logical qubits; Blue Jay: 1 billion operations on 2,000 logical qubits; qLDPC codes; Loon 2025, Kookaburra 2026, Cockatoo 2027.

title: How IBM will build the world's first large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computer
authors: Ryan Mandelbaum; Jay Gambetta; Jerry Chow; Tushar Mittal; Theodore J. Yoder; Andrew Cross; Matthias Steffen
supports: IBM blog, 10 June 2025. Gross code [[144,12,12]]: 144 data + 144 check = 288 physical qubits for 12 logical; needs long-range on-chip connections (c-couplers in Loon).

title: IBM Delivers New Quantum Processors, Software, and Algorithm Breakthroughs on Path to Advantage and Fault Tolerance
supports: Press release, 12 November 2025. Loon demonstrates key processor components for fault tolerance including longer c-couplers; real-time qLDPC decoding in under 480 ns on classical hardware; Nighthawk 120 qubits, 218 couplers, square lattice.
note: Vendor claim; not checked against peer-reviewed papers.

title: A Race Track Trapped-Ion Quantum Processor
supports: Phys. Rev. X 13, 041052 (2023). 32 qubits; average two-qubit gate infidelity 1.84(5)e-3; arbitrary connectivity via ion transport; transport ~60% of circuit time on average.

title: Realization of real-time fault-tolerant quantum error correction
supports: Phys. Rev. X 11, 041058 (2021). Ten-qubit trapped-ion QCCD machine, [[7,1,3]] color code with real-time decoding; each QEC cycle under 200 ms; physical clock (one round of random-pair gating) 10.5 ms.

title: Quantinuum Unveils Accelerated Roadmap to Achieve Universal, Fully Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing by 2030
supports: Press release, 10 September 2024. Apollo as universal, fully fault-tolerant system, 2030 in the headline; Helios as next system.

title: Quantinuum Breaks Error-Correction World Record by 10x, Validating Its Leading Path to Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing by 2029
supports: Press release, 19 October 2026 (wire copy). Claims 99.9995% logical fidelity on Helios with a color code; factor of 12 error reduction per distance step; Helix code 10 physical per logical; Apollo expected by 2029.
note: Vendor claim; underlying preprint not checked. Opened via Kyodo News PR Wire copy of the official release. This is a PR Newswire copy hosted by Kyodo; Quantinuum's own link redirects to the underlying preprint (arXiv 2610.24077), recorded separately.

title: Logical quantum processor based on reconfigurable atom arrays
supports: Nature 626, 58–65 (2024); online 6 Dec 2023. Up to 280 physical qubits; surface-code distance 3 to 7 logical gate improvement; 48 logical qubits in [[8,3,2]] codes; two-qubit fidelity 99.3–99.5%; 270 ns entangling gates; ~200 µs moves; mid-circuit readout and feedforward cycle slightly under 1 ms.

title: QuEra Computing Releases a Groundbreaking Roadmap for Advanced Error-Corrected Quantum Computers
supports: Press release, 9 January 2024. 2024: 10 logical qubits; 2025: 30 logical; 2026: 100 logical qubits and over 10,000 physical qubits.

title: QuEra Announces 2028 Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computer and Expanded Multi-Year Strategic Collaboration with AWS
supports: Press release, 15 June 2026. Libra on Amazon Braket in 2028; projected over 256 logical qubits, 1e-6 logical error rate, ~1e6 reliable logical operations.

title: A manufacturable platform for photonic quantum computing
supports: Nature 641, 876–883 (2025), doi 10.1038/s41586-025-08820-7; arXiv 2404.17570 (2024). SPAM fidelity 99.98%, HOM visibility 99.50%, two-qubit fusion fidelity 99.22%, chip-to-chip interconnect fidelity 99.72% (excluding loss).
note: Title and venue checked via Crossref; numbers from the arXiv abstract.

title: PsiQuantum Announces Omega, a Manufacturable Chipset for Photonic Quantum Computing
supports: Press release, 26 February 2025. Planned utility-scale sites in Brisbane and Chicago; rack-style cooling instead of dilution refrigerators.

title: PsiQuantum Breaks Ground on America's Largest Quantum Computing Project in Chicago
supports: Press release, 30 September 2025. Groundbreaking in Chicago for a million-qubit-scale fault-tolerant computer; no operational date given.

title: Microsoft's Majorana 1 chip carves new path for quantum computing
supports: Announcement, 19 February 2025. Eight topological qubits on a chip designed to scale to a million (company claim).

title: Interferometric single-shot parity measurement in InAs–Al hybrid devices
supports: Nature 638, 651–655 (2025), published 19 Feb 2025. Single-shot parity measurement with 1% assignment error; Peer Review File carries the editorial statement that the results do not represent evidence for Majorana zero modes.
note: Editorial statement located in the Peer Review File PDF.

title: On the robustness of topological gap detection via transport
supports: Nature 654, E22–E26 (24 June 2026), Matters Arising on Nature 638, 651. Argues the parity readout occurred in regions that appear gapless, suggesting trivial origins.

title: Reply to: On the robustness of topological gap detection via transport
supports: Nature 654, E27–E28 (24 June 2026). Microsoft maintains its measurements indicate a topological origin.

title: Google Quantum AI roadmap
supports: Six milestones; milestones 1 (2019) and 2 (2023) marked reached; milestones 3–6 undated. Viewed November 2026.

title: Quantum Echoes and verifiable quantum advantage (blog)
supports: 22 October 2025: Google states it is focused on achieving Milestone 3.

title: Unveiling our new Quantum AI campus (blog)
supports: 18 May 2021: aim to build a useful, error-corrected quantum computer within the decade.

title: Quantum error correction well below the color code threshold
authors: Ali Lavasani, Adam P. Reed, Joan M. Dreiling, et al. (Quantinuum)
supports: arXiv 2610.24077 (Oct 2026), not peer reviewed: color codes d=3,5,7; logical error as low as ~5e-6 per round; Λ = 12 (+3/−2).

title: IonQ roadmap
supports: Targets from 12 logical qubits (2026) to 80,000 logical on 2,000,000 physical (2030). Viewed November 2026; vendor plan.

title: IonQ completes acquisition of Oxford Ionics
supports: Acquisition completed 17 September 2025.

title: Trapped-ion two-qubit gates with >99.99% fidelity without ground-state cooling
authors: A. C. Hughes, R. Srinivas, C. M. Löschnauer, et al.
supports: arXiv 2510.17286 (Oct 2025), not peer reviewed: two-qubit gate error 8.4(7)×10^-5.

title: IonQ opens first dedicated quantum computing manufacturing facility in the U.S.
supports: 15 February 2024: manufacturing facility in Bothell, Washington.

title: Fault-tolerant quantum computation with a neutral atom processor
authors: Ben W. Reichardt, Adam Paetznick, David Aasen, et al. (Microsoft and Atom Computing)
supports: arXiv 2411.11822 (v1 Nov 2024, originally titled 'Logical computation demonstrated with a neutral atom quantum processor'; v3 Jun 2025): 256 Yb atoms, 24 entangled logical qubits from 48 atoms, Bernstein–Vazirani on up to 28 logical qubits. No journal reference.

title: EIFO and the Novo Nordisk Foundation acquire Magne
supports: 17 July 2025: Level 2 machine, 50 logical qubits on more than 1,200 physical qubits; Atom Computing hardware, Microsoft software; first tasks around the turn of 2026/27.

title: Repetition cat qubits for fault-tolerant quantum computation
supports: Phys. Rev. X 9, 041053 (2019): bit flips exponentially suppressed with photon number; repetition code against phase flips; bias-preserving gates.

title: Hardware-efficient quantum error correction via concatenated bosonic qubits
supports: Nature 638, 927–934 (2025): 5 cat qubits + 4 ancillas, distance-5 repetition code; bit-flip times >1 ms, phase-flip 27–33 µs; 1.65% logical error per cycle at d=5 vs 1.75% at d=3.

title: Amazon announces Ocelot quantum chip
supports: 27 February 2025: projects up to 90% less error-correction overhead for scaled machines (projection).

title: Alice & Bob quantum computing roadmap
supports: December 2024: Graphene, 100 high-fidelity logical qubits by 2030 (about 2,000 cat qubits, 1e-6 logical error per the long-form roadmap).

title: The XZZX surface code
authors: J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides; David K. Tuckett; Stephen D. Bartlett; Steven T. Flammia; Benjamin J. Brown
supports: Nature Communications 12, 2172 (2021): threshold matching the hashing bound for single-qubit Pauli noise; far fewer qubits at high bias.
